conclusion: A live public AA card on a previous resolved chain link remains legal. A live public defending AA is also legal, including one controlled by the defending player. Current weapon can be ineligible while an older AA remains eligible; this does not prohibit Lunging from being played.
derivationKind: Independent inference from exact official card target description and cited primary CR; no special current-attack limitation found.

primarySources.basis: Targets an attack action card; no current-chain-link, attacking, active-attack, ownership or controller restriction is printed.
Cards keep type/card object identities; public arena/stack objects matching the stated target description are eligible. A targeted effect fixes its targets as its layer is put on Stack.
The combat chain is public and in the arena.
Chain cards remain in the arena, attacking cards remain until they leave, a resolved chain link does not remove its AA card, and the turn player may attack again during Resolution.
Attack reaction restriction is who controls the current attack and Reaction timing; it does not restrict the printed targeted-effect description to the current attack. Source clears after resolution.
Declare legal targeted parameters before play/cost; if multiple legal cards exist, the player must be able to choose. Resolution cannot silently retarget to global active attack.
No explicit duration means a layer-continuous property effect lasts to end of turn while still applicable; no already-completed damage is recomputed.
Official indexed excerpt excludes weapon attacks. Full page403 was unavailable; no unstated wider limitation is inferred from it.
primarySources.qualification: Search excerpt only; main conclusions rely on current CR and official card text, not unavailable full ruling content.

impactOnFrozen21.qualification: The frozen21 draft is a bounded current-target subset, not complete finite target coverage. Fullblock and any case with a public defending AA has multiple legal targets and needs declaration choice.
